svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.8.8.3 Height of Guards
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.8 STAIRS, RAMPS, LANDINGS, HANDRAILS AND GUARDS
Height of Guards

g.text: Exterior, one dwelling unit, not more

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
All guards: not less than 1 070 mm (3′-6⅛″)
high
Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3).
Guards within dwelling units, or within houses
with a secondary suite including their common
spaces: not less than 900 mm (35 7/16″) high
Exterior guards serving not more than one
dwelling unit or a house with a secondary
suite: not less than 900 mm high where the
walking surface is not more than 1 800 mm
(5′-10⅞″) above finished ground
For flights of steps, guard height is measured
vertically from the top of the guard to a line
drawn through the tread nosings served
Why
Guard heights are generally based on the waist
heights of average persons. Lower heights are
permitted in dwelling units because occupants
become familiar with the hazards, and pushing and
jostling under crowded conditions is less likely.
Drawn: one house with a deck 1 500 mm up and a balcony 3 300 mm up. Heights shown are the minimums.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.8.8.3. (page 9-40), with Note A-9.8.8.3.
